articles.headline: Switching LLMs mid-conversation is a ski-rental problem

The second half of the problem is knowing when a running session should change model. This problem, which this post discusses, has a classic form: the ski-rental problem.

articles.headline: Unblockable communication with gravity
articles.blurb: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism, which is readily susceptible to screening and blocking. Gravity is a viable platform for practically unblockable communication. This study proposes and implements a wireless communication protocol where a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, and a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with an off-the-shelf, hand-held gravimeter.

articles.headline: Hardware Is Software
articles.blurb: Most hardware engineering is actually software engineering in disguise. Everything is a calculation, and calculation is software. The industry is currently doing these calculations essentially by hand, as if it were doing arithmetic without having yet discovered algebra. Hardware engineers need to design algorithms for designing their hardware. This allows small teams to build big things.

articles.headline: AWS announces ExtendDB 1.0

ExtendDB allows developers and infrastructure teams to run DynamoDB workloads in on-premise data centers, in private or public clouds, and at the edge, without rewriting application code. It is open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

articles.headline: Foundation Software

Airbnb packaged open-source Presidio, originally developed by Microsoft, as an in-process pipeline step, added domain-specific recognizers and multilingual evaluation, and then tagged de-identified datasets through its model registry. The useful pattern is turning privacy policy into testable, reusable data controls rather than asking every team to improvise.

DBTrail followed the binlog, exported initial and incremental snapshots into four open-source REST catalogs, then checked row counts and aggregates through Trino and DuckDB against MySQL. The tests surfaced real interoperability gaps around credential vending and equality deletes—not just a happy-path compatibility claim.

The resulting graph covers about 6 million datasets and helps teams trace incidents, assess the impact of changes, and safely retire unused pipelines.

articles.headline: Are we Finally Entering the Golden Age of Data Science?
articles.blurb: AI and modern data tools are making it faster to build pipelines and answer routine business questions. This gives data scientists more time to ask questions that matter, design experiments, and use AI agents to test what actually drives business outcomes.

articles.headline: Data Contracts
articles.blurb: Data contracts apply API design to datasets, describing their contents and guarantees so that people and AI agents can work with data on their own. A quality rule, such as less than 1% empty names, becomes an assertion that tooling can pass or fail. Published test results can then show how often each promise was kept.

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations. Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.
